entities.name: Cobb, Cedar, and Anderson arrive at Mandrake Falls train platform

document_metadata.title: 76、INT. COURTROOM
document_metadata.summary: Longfellow defends his plan to give land and supplies to farmers, accuses Cedar of hypocrisy, and punches him in court after accusing him of lying, causing chaos.

entities.summary: A reporter in the newsroom practices flicking a string; a girl pretends to collapse near a tree; a small-town reporter shares memories with Longfellow; Babe's true identity is revealed; a star reporter used the alias Mary Dawson to deceive Longfellow, winning a Pulitzer; someone is called by Cobb.

document_metadata.title: 76、INT. COURTROOM
document_metadata.summary: Longfellow defends his plan to give land and supplies to farmers, accuses Cedar of hypocrisy, and punches him in court after accusing him of lying, causing chaos.

entities.name: Judge consults with court experts in huddle

entities.description: The Judge addresses Longfellow directly, asking if he has anything to say before the court reaches its verdict, leaning forward to emphasize the moment.

entities.description: In response to the Judge's inquiry and Cobb's urging, Longfellow shakes his head slightly and refuses to speak, maintaining his silence during the critical moment.

entities.description: Cobb whispers to Longfellow, encouraging him to take action and not let the opposition win by remaining passive.

entities.description: The Judge declares that, based on testimony and expert recommendation, Longfellow must be committed to a medical institution for his own safety.

entities.description: A reporter comments that Longfellow is finished, reflecting the press's perception of the outcome of the trial.

entities.description: Babe stares in visible distress and fear upon hearing the Judge's ruling, showing emotional concern for Longfellow.

entities.summary: A tuba-playing man, heir to Martin W. Semple's fortune, receives legal and financial offers but remains preoccupied with band concerns, interacts with Cedar and tailors, and departs by train, waving farewell.

entities.name: Cedar
entities.description: A confident figure aligned against Longfellow, seen with clients and assistants reacting positively to the court's ruling.

entities.description: Babe leans close to Longfellow and pleads with him softly, acknowledging her past wrongs and begging him to defend himself for her sake, despite their uncertain future.

entities.description: From the witness stand, Babe explains that Longfellow's silence stems from emotional harm inflicted by the people in the town, especially herself, and that he has been exploited and ridiculed by the press.

document_metadata.title: 76、INT. COURTROOM
document_metadata.summary: Longfellow defends his plan to give land and supplies to farmers, accuses Cedar of hypocrisy, and punches him in court after accusing him of lying, causing chaos.

entities.name: Longfellow defends his decision to help struggling farmers
entities.description: From the witness stand, Longfellow explains and justifies his choice to use money to assist farmers in need rather than giving it to wealthier individuals like Mr. Cedar, using analogies about cars climbing a hill and rescuing drowning men.

entities.name: Longfellow calls on farm applicants to stand
entities.description: Longfellow addresses the courtroom audience, instructing all those who applied for a farm to stand up as evidence of the people he is trying to help.

entities.name: Farmers in courtroom stand to show need
entities.description: In response to Longfellow's request, most of the audience, primarily farmers, rise to their feet to demonstrate their participation in the farm program and their need for assistance.

entities.name: Longfellow contrasts Cedar and Semple with struggling farmers
entities.description: Longfellow points out Mr. Cedar and Mr. Semple in the courtroom, arguing they are already well-off and do not need financial help, unlike the farmers who are struggling.

entities.name: Longfellow uses rowboat analogy to justify aid priorities
entities.description: Longfellow compares his financial aid decision to choosing between rescuing a tired rower and a drowning man, arguing it is morally right to help those in greatest need.

entities.name: Courtroom Hearing In Longfellow'S Case
entities.description: A formal legal proceeding in which Longfellow testifies from the witness stand, defending his actions regarding financial aid distribution while addressing the judge, opposing parties, and an audience of farmers.
entities.summary: A formal legal proceeding in which Longfellow testifies from the witness stand, defending his actions regarding financial aid distribution while addressing the judge, opposing parties, and an audience of farmers.

entities.name: witness stand
entities.description: A physical location within the courtroom where Longfellow is testifying.

entities.name: courtroom
entities.description: The enclosed space where the hearing is taking place, containing the audience and witness stand.

entities.name: road out in front of Longfellow's house
entities.description: A specific road near Longfellow's residence, used as a metaphorical setting in his testimony.

entities.name: big boat
entities.description: A metaphorical location in Longfellow's analogy, representing his position to assist others.

entities.name: rowboat
entities.description: A small boat referenced in Longfellow's analogy, symbolizing someone who is tired but not in immediate danger.

entities.name: Longfellow Deeds
entities.description: A man testifying in court who defends his decision to allocate aid to struggling farmers by contrasting their needs with those of wealthier individuals like Mr. Cedar and Mr. Semple.
entities.summary: A tuba-playing man, heir to Martin W. Semple's fortune, receives legal and financial offers but remains preoccupied with band concerns, interacts with Cedar and tailors, and departs by train, waving farewell.

entities.name: Mr. Cedar
entities.description: An individual criticized by Longfellow during the courtroom hearing for opposing aid to struggling farmers despite not needing financial assistance himself.
entities.summary: An individual in a meeting, possibly avoiding calls, is linked to Charlie as a lawyer involved in Mr. Deeds' estate case and was criticized by Longfellow for opposing aid to struggling farmers despite personal financial stability.

entities.name: Mr. Semple
entities.description: A person mentioned by Longfellow as another example of someone who is well-off and does not need aid, unlike the struggling farmers.

entities.name: farmers in courtroom
entities.description: A group of individuals present in the courtroom who applied for farms and stand when called by Longfellow to demonstrate their need for assistance.

entities.name: farm applicants
entities.description: A group of individuals who have applied for farms and are used by Longfellow as an example of people in need of government assistance.

entities.name: cars on steep hill
entities.description: Vehicles used in Longfellow's analogy to illustrate differences in individual capacity and the need for mutual aid among people facing the same challenges.

entities.name: Longfellow reveals aid plan for farm families during testimony
entities.description: Longfellow explains his plan to provide land, livestock, and seed to farm families, contingent on three years of work, defending it as reasonable and not insane.

entities.name: Longfellow accuses Cedar of attempting to settle out of court
entities.description: Longfellow claims that Cedar tried to halt the hearing in exchange for a financial settlement, implying Cedar does not truly believe his plan is insane.

entities.name: Cedar denies attempting to settle and denounces Longfellow's plan
entities.description: Cedar angrily refutes Longfellow's claim, calling his plan a product of warped imagination and an insult to intelligence.

entities.name: Judge restores order in courtroom after Cedar's outburst
entities.description: The judge repeatedly pounds his gavel to regain control of the courtroom following Cedar's aggressive speech against Longfellow.

entities.name: Longfellow punches Cedar in the courtroom
entities.description: After finishing his testimony, Longfellow steps forward and strikes Cedar directly on the jaw, causing him to fall into the arms of his associate.

entities.name: Bailiff calls for order after Longfellow assaults Cedar
entities.description: Following Longfellow's punch, the bailiff repeatedly shouts for order as chaos erupts in the courtroom.

entities.name: Spectators react with approval to Longfellow's punch
entities.description: As Cedar is struck, members of the courtroom audience express audible approval, contributing to the pandemonium.

entities.name: front of courtroom
entities.description: The area near the entrance or exterior of the courtroom where Longfellow speaks, prior to entering the main hearing space.

entities.description: The presiding judicial officer in the courtroom who maintains order during the hearing and responds to disruptions.
entities.summary: The presiding judicial officer oversees courtroom proceedings, maintains order, consults experts, responds to disruptions, and directs legal processes, including granting permissions and making final rulings.

document_metadata.title: 77、INT. COURTROOM
document_metadata.summary: Longfellow, declared sane, is celebrated by a mob; Babe is separated but reunited when he returns, kissing passionately as the crowd cheers outside.

entities.name: Judge delivers verdict in favor of Mr. Deeds
entities.description: The Judge declares Mr. Deeds sane and dismisses the case, sparking a strong emotional reaction from everyone present in the courtroom.

entities.name: Longfellow is celebrated by supporters after the verdict
entities.description: After the case is dismissed, Longfellow is surrounded by a jubilant crowd and lifted onto the shoulders of several farmers in celebration.

entities.name: Babe attempts to reach Longfellow through the crowd
entities.description: Overcome with emotion, Babe tries to reach Longfellow but is blocked by the celebrating crowd and eventually jumps on a chair for a better view.

entities.name: Cedar reacts with disappointment to the verdict
entities.description: Cedar sits stunned after the verdict is announced, displays a grimace of dissatisfaction, and pushes Budington aside in anger.

entities.name: Mrs. Semple slaps her husband after the verdict
entities.description: In response to the outcome of the trial, Mrs. Semple expresses her frustration by slapping her husband.

entities.name: Judge warns against disturbances before announcing decision
entities.description: Before delivering the verdict, the Judge cautions all attendees that any disruptive behavior will result in arrest by police.

entities.name: Courtroom Trial Of Mr. Deeds
entities.description: A formal legal proceeding in which the sanity of Mr. Deeds is evaluated, culminating in a verdict delivered by the Judge in the presence of spectators, lawyers, and interested parties.
entities.summary: A formal legal proceeding in which the sanity of Mr. Deeds is evaluated, culminating in a verdict delivered by the Judge in the presence of spectators, lawyers, and interested parties.

entities.name: courtroom
entities.description: The physical setting where the trial of Mr. Deeds takes place, featuring a bench, aisles, and seating for spectators.

entities.summary: The presiding judicial officer oversees courtroom proceedings, maintains order, consults experts, responds to disruptions, and directs legal processes, including granting permissions and making final rulings.

entities.name: Babe Bennett
entities.description: A woman present in the courtroom who is emotionally invested in the trial's outcome and attempts to reach Longfellow after the verdict.
entities.summary: A group interacts with Longfellow during a dinner, observing and responding to social tensions; a woman performs a coin trick, claims credit for the 'Cinderella Man' story, and plans to contact Longfellow Deeds at noon.

entities.name: Longfellow Deeds
entities.description: A central figure in the trial who is acquitted by the judge and subsequently celebrated by supporters.
entities.summary: A tuba-playing man, heir to Martin W. Semple's fortune, receives legal and financial offers but remains preoccupied with band concerns, interacts with Cedar and tailors, and departs by train, waving farewell.

entities.name: Cedar
entities.description: An individual in the courtroom who reacts with disappointment and disgust following the verdict in favor of Mr. Deeds.
entities.summary: An individual accompanies Cobb and Anderson to Mandrake Falls, questions locals, attends Mrs. Meredith's inquiry about Mr. Deeds, informs Longfellow of his inheritance, introduces Cobb as a former associate, and is present at the farewell, observing the crowd and standing with Longfellow at departure.

entities.name: Mrs. Semple
entities.description: A woman who slaps her husband in anger after the verdict is announced.

entities.name: Mr. Semple
entities.description: The husband of Mrs. Semple who is slapped by her after the verdict; referred to as a 'nose-twitcher'.

entities.name: Budington
entities.description: An individual who confronts Cedar after the verdict, expressing that he had anticipated the outcome.
entities.summary: Cedar's associates include a nervous man during the meeting, another who questions delays in Power of Attorney at Cedar's desk, and a third who confronts Cedar post-verdict, claiming he anticipated the outcome.

entities.name: Bailiff
entities.description: An officer of the court who calls for order and announces the resumption of the session.

entities.name: farmers
entities.description: A group of agricultural workers whose future is directly affected by the trial's outcome; they celebrate Longfellow after the verdict.

entities.name: Longfellow is carried out of the courtroom by the crowd
entities.description: After the verdict, Longfellow is lifted and carried joyfully out of the courtroom by his excited supporters on their shoulders.

entities.name: Babe is pushed aside while trying to reach Longfellow
entities.description: As the crowd surges forward in celebration, Babe attempts to reach Longfellow but is jostled and separated from him by the mob.

entities.name: Babe is left alone and forlorn in the empty courtroom
entities.description: After the crowd leaves, Babe remains behind in the now-empty courtroom, sitting alone and visibly distressed.

entities.name: Longfellow returns to the courtroom and embraces Babe
entities.description: Hearing the commotion, Babe looks up to see Longfellow running back into the courtroom, shutting the doors behind him and rushing to sweep her into his arms.

entities.name: Babe and Longfellow share passionate kisses
entities.description: After being reunited, Babe kisses Longfellow repeatedly, and after a moment of distraction, he passionately returns her kiss.

entities.name: Falkner sisters continue whispering in the empty courtroom
entities.description: While the courtroom is otherwise empty, the Falkner sisters remain in the background, quietly whispering to each other.

entities.name: Jane
entities.description: One of the Falkner sisters who remains in the courtroom after the verdict and comments on Longfellow's behavior.
entities.summary:
